QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_9

question.text: A Cat III global-macro fund reports AUM of INR 300 crore and monthly portfolio volatility of 3.5%. Compute the 99% 1-month parametric VaR (z = 2.33).

explanation.text: The Logic: Parametric VaR under the normal-distribution assumption is VaR = z × σ × AUM. For 99% confidence, the standard one-tailed z-score is 2.33. Plugging in: VaR(99%, 1-month) = 2.33 × 3.5% × 300 cr = 2.33 × 10.50 cr ≈ INR 24.47 crore. Interpretation under the model: there is roughly a 1% probability that monthly losses exceed INR 24.47 crore. The Trap: INR 10.50 cr is just 1σ × AUM and ignores the z-multiplier entirely. INR 17.29 cr uses z = 1.645 (95% confidence), not 99%. INR 34.95 cr uses an inflated z (~3.33) with no standard interpretation. Note: The cited NISM Series XIX-E workbook pages (193, 247, 326) define VaR conceptually and discuss risk disclosure and leverage, but do not give the parametric VaR formula or the 99% z = 2.33 calculation. The formula and framing above are general quantitative-finance knowledge rather than a workbook-page citation.
